peakHours.line: Peak hours: times of day when each unit costs more under the time-of-day tariff.

story.title: The EcoProof story
story.body: Small factories burn a lot of electricity and fuel, but nobody measures their carbon, because measuring costs money. EcoProof reads the electricity bill they already get and turns it into a carbon footprint, the rupees being lost, and a plan. The quick bill fixes save money straight away. That money, plus a green loan, pays for the machines that actually cut carbon. EcoProof then proves the cut from the next bills, so the owner, the lender and the buyer can all believe it.

footer.team: Built by a team of 3 from CBIT, Hyderabad.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: Six stages, from the bill a unit already gets to proof that a lender and a buyer can check. Rupees and CO2 at every stage.

s1.title: Upload the bill
s1.short: The footprint from the bill: scope 2 from kWh, scope 1 from fuel.
s1.owner: Take a photo of the bill or upload the PDF. Add the diesel bought and the tonnes made.
s1.calc: Scope 2 = kWh x CEA grid factor. Scope 1 = fuel x its factor. On the sample bill: {{s2}} t CO2 (grid) + {{s1}} t CO2e (fuels).
s1.alt: The add-a-bill screen of the app

s2.title: Bill health
s2.short: Rupees lost on bill charges, in plain words.
s2.owner: Check each value EcoProof read; confirm it or correct it.
s2.calc: Power factor and contracted demand checks against the tariff. On the sample bill: {{inr}} a month at stake. These are bill charges, so the CO2 does not change.
s2.alt: The bill health screen of the app

s3.title: Ranked fixes
s3.short: Each fix with rupees a year and t CO2 a year, zero-cost first.
s3.owner: Pick the fixes to do and mark them planned.
s3.calc: Each fix gets rupees saved a year and t CO2 cut a year, both from the same kWh saving. The sample foundry's plan:

s4.title: Green loan summary
s4.short: EMI vs saving, and the CO2 the machine cuts.
s4.owner: Get a quote, enter the loan terms, make the summary.
s4.calc: EMI vs the low-end saving, the gap if there is one, and the t CO2 a year the machine cuts.

s5.title: Savings checked by your bills
s5.short: Rupees saved and t CO2 avoided, shown by the next bills.
s5.calc: New bills are compared with a baseline fitted to the earlier months. Until the statistics pass it says "Too early to confirm"; then "Verified by your bills".

s6.title: Share proof
s6.short: Carbon statement and loan summary with a QR; CBAM estimate for EU buyers.
s6.owner: Share a link with the lender or buyer, and see who opened it.
s6.calc: Each document carries a fingerprint and a QR that opens its verify page. EU buyers get a CBAM supplier sheet: Estimate, not verified.
s6.qr: Scan: the sample foundry's carbon statement

method.title: Carbon method
method.lead: How every number is made, worked through with the sample foundry's own figures. Each figure comes from a stored bill and a versioned factor row; none is typed in by hand.

scope2.title: Scope 2: grid electricity
scope2.formula: kWh x CEA grid factor / 1000 = t CO2
scope2.note: Location-based: the national CEA grid average. Self-used rooftop solar counts as zero.

scope1.title: Scope 1: fuel burned on site
scope1.formula: litres x fuel factor / 1000 = t CO2e
scope1.note: Open item: the per-litre diesel factor is not yet cross-checked against the IPCC per-kg value, because the diesel density was not researched.

intensity.title: Intensity per tonne of product
intensity.note: The main metric: it stays fair when production goes up or down.

action.title: CO2 cut by an action
action.formula: kWh saved a year x grid factor / 1000
action.worked: {{title}}: {{kwhLow}} to {{kwhHigh}} kWh a year x {{factor}} t/MWh = {{tLow}} to {{tHigh}} t CO2 a year
action.note: Same kWh range as the rupee saving. Bill fixes (power factor, contracted demand, peak hours) change the bill, not the carbon.

verify.title: Savings check
verify.formula: baseline: kWh = a + b x tonnes, fitted to earlier months
verify.note: Needs at least {{months}} months and must fit within CV(RMSE) {{cv}}% and NMBE ±{{nmbe}}% (ASHRAE Guideline 14 monthly limits). Until then it says "Too early to confirm"; after, "Verified by your bills" (EcoProof's own method, not a third-party check).

notCounted.title: What is not counted
notCounted.embodied: Embodied carbon in the metal, machines and buildings.
notCounted.scope3: Scope 3: the supply chain, such as purchased pig iron and scrap.
notCounted.gases: Other gases from the grid: the CEA factor is CO2 only, so grid totals say t CO2 and fuel totals say t CO2e.

limits.title: Honest limits
limits.grid: The grid factor is a national average, not the mix of one DISCOM or one hour.
limits.synthetic: The demo bills are synthetic: they show the method, not a real unit.
limits.household: Household rupees leave out FSA and electricity duty.
limits.self: The savings check uses the unit's own bills. It is not a third-party verification.

lenders.title: For lenders
lenders.lead: A short, bill-backed summary for green and energy-efficiency loans to small units, with the carbon the loan cuts.
lenders.big: EcoProof does not lend. It prepares a summary for the lender's own assessment.

gets.title: What a lender gets
gets.bills: Bill evidence: up to 12 months of confirmed bills, each with its source line.
gets.range: A saving range (low to high) from the unit's own bills, not one optimistic number.
gets.emi: EMI vs the low-end saving, and the gap if there is one.
gets.co2: The t CO2 a year the machine cuts, on the same kWh basis as the rupees.
gets.qr: A QR that opens the verify page, to check the document was not changed.

why.title: Why it helps green lending
why.body: Banks want proof that a saving is real before they lend for efficiency. A full energy assessment is costly for a small unit. This summary uses the unit's own bills, and after the loan the next bills show whether the saving happened.

schemes.note: Pointers only. Terms change: confirm with the lender or the scheme office.

sidbi.name: SIDBI 4E
sidbi.body: Energy-efficiency loans: repayment up to 84 months including up to 12 months moratorium; the rate is MCLR-linked. SIDBI's own pages differ on the terms, so use the live sidbi.in values.

gift.name: MSE-GIFT
gift.body: 2% a year interest subvention for up to 5 years on term loans up to ₹2 crore, for Udyam micro and small units. The machine must be on the scheme's technology list.

zed.name: Bank concessions for ZED
zed.body: Some banks publish lower rates or fees for units with ZED certification (for example SBI and SIDBI: Bronze 5 bps plus 5% off the processing fee). They are lender-published, vary by level and carry no date: ask the bank.

cbam.title: CBAM supplier sheet
cbam.body: For EU importers: emissions per tonne of iron and steel goods, from the supplier's fuel and electricity records, in an Excel sheet.
cbam.direct: For iron and steel, the sheet covers direct emissions only.
cbam.verifier: Verified data must be confirmed by an accredited verifier.

scope.title: Which castings CBAM covers
scope.now: In scope now: cast iron pipes (CN 7303) and cast fittings (CN 7307 11, 7307 19).
scope.later: Most castings (CN 7325, other cast articles of iron or steel) are not in scope today. They are only proposed for CBAM from 1 January 2028 (COM(2025) 989, not yet adopted).
scope.note: Source: EU CBAM goods list and the Commission proposal, as summarised in EcoProof research R4.

homes.title: For homes
homes.lead: Rooftop solar, the PM Surya Ghar subsidy and the home's own bills, priced on the TGSPDCL LT-I domestic slabs, with the CO2 avoided each year.
homes.slabs: Bills are priced on the TGSPDCL LT-I domestic slabs (FY 2026-27).
homes.after: After solar: {{months}} months of bills, {{inr}} saved against the same months last year.
